get.description: List all asynchronous operations for the company. Non-admin users only see operations they created, unless the request is filtered to a company-readable operation type (for example `bulk_create_and_initialize_projects`) — either directly via `operation_type` or via `parent_id` — in which case matching operations are returned with a restricted payload that omits `result`, `error`, and `created_by_id`.

parameters.name: parent_id
parameters.description: Return child operations of the specified parent operation.

parameters.name: filters[operation_type]
parameters.description: Return operations of the specified type.

parameters.name: filters[started_after]
parameters.description: Return operations that started after the started_after time.

parameters.name: filters[started_before]
parameters.description: Return operations that started before the started_before time.

parameters.name: filters[status]
parameters.description: Return operations with the specified status.

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

result.description: Operation-specific result.  See the initiating API for details on the result format.

context.description: Opaque internal context information for the operation.

created_by_id.description: User ID of the user who created the operation

project_id.description: ID of the project the operation belongs to, if any

parent_id.description: ID of the parent operation, if this operation is a child of a batch operation

failure_details.description: Why this operation failed, when the failure was recorded with a reason. Populated for rows of a bulk create that were rejected before a project was attempted, or that failed while initializing. Null for operations that did not fail this way.

submitted_row.description: Values submitted for this row, keyed by bulk-create template column. Restricted to the name and project_number columns for readers who are neither the operation creator nor a company admin.

row_index.description: Zero-based position of this row in the original bulk-create upload. Present on failed create_and_initialize_project children so clients can label the row and restore upload order. Children are not created in upload order — pre-flight rejects are inserted after executed rows — so created_at is not a substitute.

code.description: HTTP status in screaming snake case (like BAD_REQUEST)

reason_code.description: A machine-readable code that identifies the error specifically enough for the client to interpret what happened and take action.

x-changelog.description: Add a new filter to the asynchronous operations list endpoint to filter child operations by their parent operation id. The parent_id field is now also included in operation responses.

x-changelog.description: Add a new filter to the asynchronous operations list endpoint to filter operations by project_id.

x-changelog.summary: Add new v2 asynchronous operations list endpoint
x-changelog.description: Add a new v2 endpoint to get a list of asynchronous operations for a company.

x-changelog.summary: Add created_by_id to asynchronous operations list response
x-changelog.description: Added created_by_id field to the asynchronous operations list response to identify the user who created the operation.

x-changelog.summary: Add failure_details to asynchronous operations list response
x-changelog.description:
Added an optional failure_details field to the asynchronous operations list response, matching the
field added to the details response. This field is populated for operations that failed with a
recorded reason and contains an errors array of failure reasons, a submitted_row object
holding the values that were submitted, and a row_index integer for the row's 0-based position
in the original bulk-create upload. Operations that did not fail this way return null. Readers
who are neither the operation creator nor a company admin receive submitted_row restricted to the
name and project_number columns; errors and row_index are returned in full because showing
reasons to company readers is the purpose of the field.

x-changelog.summary: Return the unrestricted view when listing children of an operation you created
x-changelog.description:
Filtering the asynchronous operations list by parent_id now returns the unrestricted payload when
the requesting user created the parent operation, matching the entitlement the details endpoint
already grants a creator. Previously a creator who was not a company admin was served the
restricted company-readable payload, which omits result, error, and created_by_id.
